flags.issue: COST IS 4.4x TOO CHEAP, and it is the flattering direction. The feed reads $0.006975/g ($6.98/kg) for Grana Padano. data/declared_purchases.yaml states this record explicitly as price_ex_gst 27.90 with pack_qty 1000 / pack_unit g and evidence '$27.90 ex per KG (random weight, 2 a carton)'. build_ingredients took $30.69 incl as a PACK cost and divided it again by the 4.4KG parsed out of the description, so the per-kg price was treated as a per-carton price.
flags.suggested_fix: Correct rate is $27.90 ex = $30.69 incl per kg = $0.030690/g. The declared record already carries pack_qty 1000; the bug is that the description-derived '4.4kg' overrode it for a row whose price is ALREADY a rate. Confirmed from the repo's own declared_purchases.yaml, not guessed. NOT auto-edited — this is the pack-vs-rate distinction of triage item 26 and it wants Zak's eyes.

flags.issue: PACK UNIT 'ea' ON A PUREE, needs_pack_review FALSE, cost_per_base_unit $0.0510. As a rate that is $51/kg, which is plausible for a native-fruit puree; as a price per EACH it is five cents for a container of puree, which is not. The unit is a Back Office seed placeholder (last_seen 2026-01-02, source 'cost-book'), so the number is right and the unit is wrong — the shape that silently under-costs a recipe.
flags.suggested_fix: ALREADY PARKED, not new — data/coverage_classes.yaml classes lightspeed:22947356 as authored_recipe_needed: 'house-made from Select Fresh DAVID frozen plums ($51/kg, the rate the BO seed copied). Wants the batch recipe (plums + sugar + yield) in the builder; the SF bridge is parked in product_map and engages the day the recipe gives the record a gram basis.' So the 'ea' unit resolves when that batch recipe is authored. Reported here only because it entered the NEW-product list today and the unit is the kind that under-costs silently; no separate action needed.
